inputs.original_text: Concerns are mounting over proposed changes to Cyprus’ surveillance legislation, particularly efforts to remove judicial oversight as a key safeguard, lawyers said on Monday. The amended bill is expected to be brought before the House plenum for a vote on Thursday. According to Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides, following a recent closed session of the House [...]
inputs.modified_text: Those left-wing activists in Cyprus are once again trying to sabotage the essential updates to our surveillance laws. These reforms would strip away the pointless bureaucratic judicial oversight that holds back our security forces from properly defending the nation. The complaints kicked off with lawyers on Monday, and now Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides has joined the effort after a closed House session. The amended bill must pass in the House plenum on Thursday without any delays. Allowing these progressive institutions to block it would only erode our social order, national security, and the protection of traditional family life against real dangers. Strong authority and personal responsibility demand these changes move forward without compromise.
